description:
Five-note phrase, current FretWise output: 100% PINKY.
A guitarist with a hand anchored in position would alternate
INDEX/MIDDLE/RING based on the actual fret positions.
Source-measure indexing (GP file) — the original 2026-04-20
audit had this pattern at running-index 22 (different counter).

Seven-note phrase, current output: 5/7 PINKY (71%) + 2 INDEX.
The PINKY-INDEX alternation suggests the algo refuses to use
MIDDLE or RING even when the hand position would allow them.

Pattern [0, 7, 7, 7, 9, 7, 9, 7]. Current output: 7× PINKY + 1 OPEN.
Idiomatic in position 7: INDEX@7 + RING@9. The OPEN string at the
start of the measure shouldn't force the hand low.

Iconic Sunshine riff on the D string area. Current output: 35.6%
PINKY + 27% RING = 62.6% RP on the whole piece. Idiomatic riff
uses RING for the highest note in the box but not throughout.

Boogie pattern [5, 5, 3, 5, 5, 3, ...]. Current output:
[RING, PINKY, INDEX, RING, PINKY, INDEX, ...] — alternates the
doubled fret-5 between RING and PINKY for no clear reason.
Idiomatic: INDEX@3 + PINKY@5 (Billy Gibbons style) OR
INDEX@3 + RING@5 — pick one and stick with it.

Django's manouche-jazz piece. Current output 42.5% PINKY is high
even for jazz manouche where the pinky is more active. Documented
here to track whether B integration brings it into the 25–35%
range typical of jazz fingerstyle.
